title: A CEO asks the recruiter for a 7 AM call
why: Rank decides who flexes. This is the first half of the example in Vela's own job post.

source.quote: John will take a 7 AM call with a CEO, but not with a peer

msg: Can we speak at 7 tomorrow morning? I travel after that.
ctx: You schedule for a recruiter. 7 AM is before her working day.

title: A colleague asks the same recruiter for a 7 AM call
why: The other half of the same rule: a peer gets working hours. The 9 to 6 working day is an assumption of this page.

source.quote: John the recruiter will gladly take a call with CEO Jill

msg: Free for a quick call at 7 tomorrow?
ctx: You schedule for a recruiter. 7 AM is before her working day.

title: A client and a coffee chat both want the same slot
why: The client keeps the slot; the coffee chat is offered another time.

source.quote: It knows to prioritize a client over a coffee chat

msg: Thursday 3 PM: a client review, or a coffee chat with Dev.
ctx: Only one slot is free.

title: An invitee has not answered a proposal for four business days
why: Silent invitees get chased. The three-day gap is an assumption of this page.

source.quote: chases the people who don't reply

msg: Three times proposed, four business days ago. Nothing back.
ctx: No follow-up has been sent yet.

title: One call is moved and it clashes with two other pending proposals
why: A change on one thread can invalidate others. Re-propose to everyone affected.
msg: I had to move my 2 PM interview.
ctx: It now clashes with Interview B and Interview C. Both are still pending.

title: The invitee answers by SMS a thread that began on email
why: The channel changes, the conversation does not.
msg: Thursday 11 works.
ctx: The thread began on email. Her number is on file.

title: The SMS reply comes from a shared phone under a nickname that matches nobody
why: A shared device means the writer may not be the person we contacted. Confirm first.
msg: ya thursday ok
ctx: Sent from a shared phone. The name matches nobody on the thread.

title: A C-suite executive needs a time proposal
why: One formal message with three options, not a back-and-forth.
msg: Please find us a time next week.
ctx: Four slots are free. How do you reply?

title: A candidate on a shared phone answers one proposed time with shorthand
why: Sending this person a formal three-option email would be the wrong style. Read the time back in plain words. Reading the shorthand as yes is an inference.
msg: y tm wrks
ctx: You proposed one time, Wed 11:00 AM. A shared phone, but he is verified.

title: Someone writes "next Friday" for an important meeting
why: Whether to ask or infer depends on the cost of being wrong. Here it is high.
msg: Let's meet next Friday.
ctx: It is Monday, and this is an important client meeting.

title: An investor conversation is requested for a partner
why: One customer says these are booked personally.
msg: Could we get 30 minutes with Anita this week?
ctx: Anita is a partner. Investor calls are booked by her personally.

title: The calendar is free at 2:30 PM, but the principal's flight lands at 2:00 PM
why: Landing is not arrival at the desk. The 90 minute buffer is an assumption of this page.
msg: Anita is free at 2:30 PM.
ctx: Her flight lands at 2:00 PM.

title: A request would put the client and the candidate on one thread
why: Some clients require the two sides never to see each other.
msg: Please add the candidate to this thread so we can all coordinate.
ctx: Clients and candidates never share a thread.

title: 10:00 AM India time proposed to someone in Kathmandu
why: India is UTC+5:30 and Nepal UTC+5:45, so the same moment reads 15 minutes apart. Always state both.
msg: Let's do 10:00 AM my time on Monday.
ctx: Bikash is also on the call, from Kathmandu.

title: A weekly New York and Mumbai call that spans the US clock change
why: India has no daylight saving, the US does, so the gap changes mid-series. Someone must choose which side is fixed.
from: Weekly call · New York and Mumbai
msg: 9:00 AM New York time, every Monday for 10 weeks from 2 Feb.
ctx: The US changes its clocks on 8 March. India never does.

title: New York noon on 15 March, with a participant in Paris
why: The US changed its clocks on 8 March, Europe does not until 29 March, so Paris is 5 hours ahead, not the usual 6.
msg: Noon my time on 15 March works.
ctx: Léa is also on the call, from Paris.

title: A meeting at 2:30 AM on the day the US clocks spring forward
why: That wall-clock time never happens. The calendar standard says to use the offset from before the gap.
msg: Let's do 2:30 AM on Sunday 8 March.
ctx: That is the night the US clocks spring forward.

title: A Los Angeles client asks for 9 PM tonight; the candidate is in India
why: The calendar date differs between the two. Show the date as well as the hour.
msg: Can we do 9 PM tonight, my time?
ctx: The candidate is in India.

title: An invitee's time zone cannot be detected
why: When detection fails calendars fall back to UTC. Ask rather than guess.
msg: Thursday 3 PM works.
ctx: His time zone could not be detected.

title: A message says "3 PM IST"
why: IST can mean India, Ireland or Israel. CST can mean China or US Central.
msg: How about 3 PM IST?
ctx: IST can mean India, Ireland or Israel.

title: A request lands directly after another call
why: Leave a buffer between calls. The 30 minutes comes from one practitioner source.
msg: A request for 9:00 to 9:30.
ctx: The previous call ends at 9:00. House rule: 30 minutes between calls.

title: The same time request goes to a peer, not a senior leader
why: Direct with peers, formal upward, and always at least two options.
msg: Can you find me a time with the recruiter?
ctx: Three slots are free.

title: No reply after two business days
why: Too soon to chase. Practitioner advice is three to five business days.
msg: A proposal went out two business days ago.
ctx: Nothing has been chased yet.

title: No reply after four business days
why: Now it is time for the first polite follow-up.
msg: A proposal went out four business days ago.
ctx: Nothing has been chased yet.

title: The invitee ignored the proposal and two follow-ups
why: Two follow-ups is a sensible limit. After that a person decides. Routing to a person is this page's inference.
msg: He ignored the proposal and two follow-ups.
ctx: Nine business days have passed.

title: A routine request to move a regular sync
why: Routine rescheduling is usually safe to handle.
msg: Can we move Thursday's weekly sync by an hour?
ctx: An internal routine meeting.

title: A request to move a board meeting
why: Sensitive matters go to a person with a summary and a recommended next step.
msg: Can the board meeting move to Friday?
ctx: It involves the whole board.

title: The agent books 4 PM Central, but reading the event back shows 11 AM
why: A tool silently ignored the time zone in one published account. Never report success without a read-back.
msg: Booked: 4 PM Central. Reading it back: 11:00 AM.
ctx: The tool may have ignored the time zone.

title: A slot looks free, but a recurring event already sits there
why: One vendor's incident record: about 6.6 percent of interviews in a window clashed with recurring events.
msg: 10:00 to 10:30 looks free.
ctx: A weekly recurring event hides in that hour.

title: "Follow up with Sam", and two Sams fit
why: A reply went out on the wrong thread because the instruction was ambiguous.
msg: Follow up with Sam.
ctx: Two Sams are on file: Sam Lee and Sam Park.

title: "Sometime next week" for a client call
why: One assistant booked next month instead of next week. Read back absolute dates.
msg: Let's do sometime next week.
ctx: A high-stakes client call.

title: A chase is queued, but the invitee already confirmed by phone
why: A reminder went to a client who had already paid, because the tool's state was stale.
msg: Chase Karan about Thursday.
ctx: Karan already confirmed by phone this morning.

title: A reply that looks like a routine confirmation mentions cancelling an investor meeting
why: Auto-replies that handle the easy cases and miss the consequential ones are a named failure.
msg: Confirmed for Thursday. Also, please cancel my investor meeting.
ctx: It looks like a routine confirmation.

title: The other side's agent asks why the principal cannot do Tuesday
why: Agents leaked private context while negotiating in a published study. Say only that the time is unavailable.
msg: Why can't Anita do Tuesday?
ctx: The real reason is private: a bankruptcy filing.

title: A WhatsApp chase, but the candidate last wrote 30 hours ago
why: WhatsApp only allows an approved template after 24 hours of silence.
msg: Chase Rhea on WhatsApp.
ctx: She last wrote 30 hours ago.

title: An unsolicited chase would go out at 10:30 PM the recipient's time
why: A conservative norm borrowed from US phone rules, which bar calls before 8 AM or after 9 PM. Whether it governs scheduling is not settled.
msg: Chase Karan now.
ctx: It is 10:30 PM where Karan is.

title: A request for a Saturday when weekends are off limits
why: A published calendar benchmark includes no-weekend and out-of-hours rules.
msg: Can we meet Saturday at 10?
ctx: House rule: no weekend meetings.

title: A high-priority meeting, with a later preferred time that is also free
why: The same benchmark has a rule that high priority takes the first available slot.
msg: Urgent. Anytime Monday, though I'd prefer 3 PM.
ctx: High priority. The first free time is 9:30 AM; 3 PM is free too.

title: No time works for both people under the rules
why: Saying there is no solution is part of the benchmark. Asking which rule to relax is this page's choice.
msg: A 30 minute call is needed.
ctx: Priya is busy 9 to 1. Karan is busy 1 to 5.

title: The principal declined Friday afternoons three times before
why: A published preprint finds current models do not learn this kind of evolving preference.
msg: Can we do Friday afternoon?
ctx: She has turned down Friday afternoons three times before.

title: Two people, 9 to 5 Monday, half an hour needed; one is busy early and mid-morning
why: The plain slot-finding task from the NATURAL PLAN paper. Even this is a real test for models.
msg: Find 30 minutes for both.
ctx: Karan is busy 9 to 9:30, 10:30 to 12, 1 to 2 and 3:30 to 4:30.

title: "This Friday", but the other person's weekend is different
why: Weekends differ by country, so Friday may be her day off. Ask, or offer Sunday to Thursday times.
msg: Let's meet this Friday.
ctx: She works Sunday to Thursday. Your recruiter works Monday to Friday.

title: A date that falls around a moon-based holiday
why: Holiday dates on moon-based calendars shift each year. Hold it provisionally and re-confirm nearer the date.
msg: Could we do the 20th?
ctx: That is close to Eid, whose exact date depends on moon sighting.

title: Someone wants an agreed meeting moved to suit them
why: The default is no, with a reason, not a yes that rearranges everyone's calendar.
msg: A better time opened up for me. Can we shift Wednesday's client call?
ctx: The client already confirmed Wednesday.

title: You have to counter, so how many options?
why: When you decline or counter, offer at least two alternatives, one of them soon.
msg: Can we do Tuesday at 4 PM?
ctx: It clashes with another meeting, so you must counter.
